alignments.note: Recitative ὅτι, marked in English by quotation rather than by a word (rule 43). A reference comparison will report this as a disagreement.
Compound εἰσέρχομαι: subject pronoun and the preverb's particle in ride inside the verb's unit; the expressed πρός has its own word, so nothing competes for in (rules 9 and 106).

Greek expresses both elements of the support pair ἀκροβυστίαν ἔχοντας and the ASV collapses them into the single word uncircumcised, so the two tokens are one unit; the source head is the noun the English word realizes (rule 73).
Auxiliary rides with the lexical verb; the compound's dative complement takes the English preposition under rule 106's oblique arm, an English verb word being written for the compound.

Dative object with the English preposition realizing its case government, as ACT.4.1 and ACT.4.3 read the same shape (rules 21 and 106). Keeping with inside the verb's unit as the preverb's own realization remains defensible.

review_notes: The dative αὐτοῖς takes with them on the oblique-case arm of rule 106; the competing reading gives with to the preverb συν-.
ἀκροβυστίαν ἔχοντας treated as a collapsed support pair under rule 73.
